comment: Reviewer notes read by report.mjs: a rough gap class per asset from the baseline run of Nov 4, 2026 (typescript-usd main renderer, Safari, 512 px) against OpenUSD 26.11.1 usdrecord. Classes: match, geometry, material/shading, texture sampling, lighting, colour space, unsupported feature, crash. These are readings of the images and diagnostics, not computed results; re-check them when the numbers move.
harness: Camera-light ambient: usdrecord's camera light has ambient 0.01 (frameRecorder.cpp:442); usdview's has none (stageView.py:1459-1465). The viewer follows usdview; the harness captures each asset twice, with usdview's lighting (browser.png, compared with usdview.png) and with the lighting state usdrecord's frame recorder hands the engine (runtime.setLightingSource('frameRecorder'), src/frame-recorder-lighting.ts; browser-usdrecord.png, compared with native.png and scored). Nov 6, 2026: subdiv_catmull_clark and the fallback-material corpus scenes then match usdrecord (0 px); the old --material-ambient 0.4 experiment is superseded.
Alpha: usdrecord clears to (0,0,0,0); the viewer canvas is opaque black. RGB is compared; native alpha is only a coverage mask.

Camera light, MSAA 4x (HDX_MSAA_SAMPLE_COUNT default and the viewer's sampleCount), sRGB output, purposes, time and complexity are matched by setting; GPU frustum culling is left at each renderer's default (it should not change pixels).

The scene is framed from bounds of default+proxy purposes at the start time; assets whose bounds include an environment (StandardShaderBall) are seen from outside it, so their shading is not exercised.
Timings are not like for like: native is usdrecord wall time (python start, open, render, write); browser open is runtime.open() with payloads loaded, settled is until two identical captures.
Nondeterminism seen once: in one of five browser runs McUsd rendered with darker textures (19.7% instead of 10.05%); four repeats reproduced 10.05%. Re-run before trusting a single change on McUsd.
Safari must stay visible: when its window was hidden/occluded, a harness iframe stalled for over 20 minutes (timers throttled) and the run had to be resumed for the last two assets.

shaderball.summary: Matches, but the framing shows the outside of the environment box, not the MaterialX shader ball; native posts one hdSt warning (missing mtlximage2 texture).

brainstem.summary: A handful of silhouette pixels differ (max 11); PSNR 63 dB.

subdiv_catmull_clark.summary: Differed from usdrecord only by the camera-light ambient; with usdrecord's lighting state (browser-usdrecord.png) 0 px differ (Nov 6, 2026).

normals_types.summary: With usdrecord's lighting (Nov 6, 2026) the camera-light-ambient difference is gone; 365 px remain on meshes whose points or normals count does not match the topology, which the viewer rejects ('Invalid Hydra prim ... Vertex primvar ... has N elements') and native draws.

teapot.summary: Specular highlight on UsdPreviewSurface is larger/brighter than native (max 73).

bike.summary: Metallic rims and brake discs differ (specular response); native also reports 7 invalid-primvar warnings (too many vertex primvar elements) the viewer does not post.

elephant.summary: Fine texture detail differs at grazing angles (mip/anisotropic filtering).

animated_cube.summary: Same colour on average; the viewer's texture is blurrier at grazing angles (native looks anisotropically filtered).

mcusd.summary: Native renders the pixel-art textures crisp; the viewer filters them smoothly (sampler filter/mip differences).

damaged_helmet.summary: Viewer is brighter overall (mean RGB +4) on metallic/rough PBR surfaces; emissive matches.

texture_transform.summary: Lower row of panels is lit differently (backside/normal or specular); the UsdTransform2d results themselves agree.

mtlx_basic.summary: Matches usdrecord (0 significant px, 3 runs, Nov 5 2026) since Storm meshes the implicit sphere through HdsiImplicitSurfaceSceneIndex, as native does.

alpha_blend_mode.summary: The 'Opaque' label's checkmark texture renders black in the viewer instead of green over white; translucent panels differ slightly.

chess.summary: Pawn heads (glossy dark spheres in native) render flat black in the viewer; board and other pieces close.

roughness.summary: Roughness ramp rows are lit very differently (native shows bright grazing specular on the lower rows and a backdrop the viewer leaves dark; coverage differs by 12k pixels).

normals_bias_scale.summary: Normal-map bias/scale cards close; small differences on the edges of bumped regions.

curves.summary: Features-group baseline (Nov 5, 2026, 3 runs): the viewer fails to open the scene ("/World/BSplineOpen: widths vertex cardinality does not match topology"); native draws linear and cubic curves.

points.summary: Features-group baseline: points render; 626 px differ (0.24%), on point edges and sizes.

pi_basic.class: unsupported feature (curves in an instanced scene)
pi_basic.summary: Features-group baseline: the instanced shapes agree within 2/255; the differing pixels are the scene's axis curves, which the viewer does not draw.

ni_cubes.summary: Features-group baseline: all eight native instances are drawn; the unlit sides of the cubes differ, as for the other fallback-material assets.

skel_arm.summary: Features-group baseline: native draws the arm bent at frame 7; the viewer draws it in its rest pose (88,668 px, 33.8%).

subdiv_refined.summary: Features-group baseline: the viewer fails ("unsupported refinement level 3; supported levels are 0, 1, 2"). The upstream test uses complexity 1.4 (level 4); the harness's closest setting is veryhigh (1.3, level 3).

volumes.class: unsupported feature (glslfx volume and translucent shaders)
volumes.summary: Features-group baseline: the viewer refuses the scene ("TranslucentTagMat: unsupported surface shader (missing info:id)"), so no volume is drawn.

vdb_volume.summary: Features-group baseline: the viewer refuses the scene ("CheckerboardMaterial: unsupported surface shader (missing info:id)") before the OpenVDB fields are read.
